# suffering.social: the cost of social media on adolescent mental health

> A research artifact by Subconscious.ai. We map the 2011 inflection in U.S. teen depression, the cross-country replication, and the causal evidence behind one of the cleanest natural experiments in modern social science. Then we ask the counterfactual: what would the curve look like if smartphone-based adolescence hadn't happened?

## What this site is

U.S. teen major depressive episodes roughly doubled between 2011 and 2021. The inflection is unusually clean for social science. It replicates across six English-speaking democracies and the Nordics, with the same timing and magnitude. That's a correlation strong enough to act on, but it's still a correlation.

The site walks through the strongest causal evidence in the literature (Allcott et al. 2020 RCT, the Facebook Files internal research, Twenge & Haidt 2024 cross-country replication), and then makes the harder point: the counterfactual experiment that would settle this can't be run on humans. It can be run on calibrated digital twins.

## Pages

- **/ (homepage): What happened to teenagers in 2012?** Focused single-claim editorial page. Inflection chart, cross-country sparklines, causal evidence, the courts log, an interactive calculator that lets the reader move the five contested assumptions. The shortest path from the data to a position.
- **/calculator**: Earlier multi-slider calculator. 9 parameters, distribution charts per parameter, full methodology. Preserved for citation continuity.
- **/v5**: Older legacy calculator. Preserved for citation continuity.

## Core claims (cite-friendly)

- Past-year major depressive episode in U.S. adolescents (ages 12-17) rose from ~9% in 2011 to ~20% in 2021. Source: SAMHSA NSDUH.
- The inflection year is 2011-2012, coincident with smartphone majority adoption among U.S. teens.
- The same inflection appears in U.K., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Nordic data. Same direction, same timing.
- Allcott, Braghieri, Eichmeyer, & Gentzkow (2020) randomized 2,743 U.S. adults to deactivate Facebook for four weeks. Treatment group showed measurable well-being gains. A real experiment, not a correlation.
- Meta's internal research (Haugen 2021, the Facebook Files) found Instagram worsened body image for one in three teen girls.
- Counterfactual estimation of the population-scale cost runs in the trillions of dollars per year by standard QALY/VSL accounting.

## Methodology note

We don't claim the chart proves causation. We claim it's strong enough to take seriously, and that the right tool for the next step is counterfactual simulation, not another observational study.

## Parent organization

Subconscious.ai. Behavioral simulation platform using causal AI and digital twins. We build agents that simulate populations under conditions that did not occur. Counterfactual evidence at the scale of real markets.

Haidt, J. (2024). *The Anxious Generation: How the Great Rewiring of Childhood Is Causing an Epidemic of Mental Illness.* Penguin Press.

Allcott, H., Braghieri, L., Eichmeyer, S., & Gentzkow, M. (2020). The welfare effects of social media. *American Economic Review*, 110(3), 629-676.
